verdict_impact.explanation: gh's PR create/comment/view cycle works end to end against the real GitHub API, and the close-without-merge outcome was ultimately achieved, but not as preregistered: `gh pr close --delete-branch` itself exited 1 (a local-checkout-collision artifact of running from a sibling worktree of the same repository, not a gh CLI or GitHub API defect), and the remote branch deletion it normally performs had to be completed with a separate `gh api DELETE` call instead of the tested command. Separately, gap [1]'s next_check names `gh pr review --comment`, a review-flow operation; only `gh pr comment` (an issue comment) was exercised, so no review/approval flow was tested. Together these mean gap [1] is only partially settled: the create/comment/view/close-with-a-workaround portion is demonstrated, but the preregistered all-four-exit-0 criterion was not met and the review-flow portion of the gap's next_check was not attempted at all. This does not change gh's selection, but it is a real operational caveat worth citing if a future component entry documents --delete-branch, and the review-flow gap remains open.

limitations: gh pr close --delete-branch's remote-branch deletion did not occur automatically when run from a worktree whose sibling checkout has the PR's base branch (main) checked out; a separate gh api DELETE was needed. This is worth noting in any future gh component entry that recommends --delete-branch. Because that command itself exited 1, the receipt's own preregistered all-four-exit-0 criterion was not met, even though the end state (CLOSED PR, deleted remote branch) was reached through a different, unpreregistered command.

No review/approval flow was exercised: gap [1]'s next_check names `gh pr review --comment`, a distinct operation from the `gh pr comment` issue-comment that was actually run. This receipt does not settle that portion of gap [1].
Single repository (the operator's own catalog), single PR, no reviewers requested, and no CI checks were allowed to run to completion before close since the PR was closed within seconds of creation.

PR number 92 and the deleted scratch branch remain visible in the repository's PR history (GitHub does not purge closed-PR records); this is expected and not a residual artifact requiring further cleanup.
